minutes.headline: Committee unanimously approved the final capital rankings, with the DPW's second front-end loader ranked 23rd of 35.
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee heard a last-minute plea from the DPW director for a second front-end loader, then discussed the full ranked list of 35 requests and voted on the final ranking after fixing a duplicated rank. Members also approved three sets of prior minutes, agreed to start long-term (five-year) capital planning in January, and discussed the charter-driven December deadline.

public_comment.topic: DPW director pitched the front-end loader as his number one capital priority, citing a storm-day breakdown of the backhoe while the loader was in for repairs.
A resident of Reservoir Road remarked that the DPW lacks an air compressor and offered use of their own jackhammer and compressor.

votes.motion: Approve the final capital request rankings as presented, after correcting the duplicated rank.
Approve minutes of November 20, November 29 and December 4.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the plan means buying a second loader and maintaining two rather than one.
The DPW director said renting a loader is hard and expensive.
The loader landed below the midpoint of the ranked list.
Members computed a running cost total down the list to find roughly where funding would reach halfway.
Members discussed the cost tied to the permit expiring and the engineering already hired, funded in the current year's capital plan.
It is unknown how much capital funding there will be; the town manager decides in the preliminary budget.

decisions.decision: DPW director to sit down with some members to develop a plan for the second loader; revisit in the long-term capital plan after the New Year.
Long-term five-year capital planning meetings to start around mid or late January, with dates to be posted.
Chair to review the charter provision requiring the December timing of the capital plan.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee voted unanimously, by voice, to approve the final capital request rankings after fixing a duplicated rank.
The DPW director's request for a second front-end loader ranked below the midpoint of the 35 ranked requests, and the ranking was not changed.
The DPW director will sit down with some members to develop a plan for the second loader, to be revisited in the long-term capital plan after the New Year.
Members agreed to start five-year capital planning meetings around mid or late January, with dates to be posted.
The chair will review the charter provision that sets the December timing of the capital plan.

why_it_matters: The ranked list is the order in which capital requests, such as equipment and the Marshall Pond permit work, would be funded, so where a request falls decides whether it is likely to be paid for.
How much capital money there will be is not yet known and is set by the town manager in the preliminary budget, so a request's rank is not a promise of funding.
